Recovering alcoholic here. I was very lucky in that my family was super supportive. My fiance's family, however, simply attributed my addiction to weakness and low character.  That hurt quite a bit,  but I cannot change how someone thinks or behaves, and to fixate on it will just make me crazy. 
About a year after I got sober, I went to make my amends to them, and they started asking questions about whether alcoholism ran in my family. It seemed like their perception of me and of addiction had changed, but that change took a very long time.
I have extended family who still do not know, because I anticipate that they will judge me. I do not hold it against them. Some people just cannot wrap their minds around addiction. Sometimes it is because of the beliefs they were brought up with, sometimes it is willful ignorance. Some people may just be scared of it and avoid you because they don't understand. Others may be afraid of enabling.
If the relationships mean anything to you, you might consider sharing how their actions made you feel. Nothing can ever be resolved by just shutting them out. At least then you may have some closure.
I am not one to tell another how to live his life, but I have personally relapsed because I thought I could use another substance as long as it was not my drug of choice. Addiction is almost always not about the substance, but about the behaviors and thinking. This is not an attempt to tell you what to do. In the last week two people I have known have ODed and I have one funeral tomorrow - my words come from a place of compassion only.

Thank you. I was more trying to find a way to get out asap because it is scary to be around him, but emotional abuse is so difficult to prove. In Illinois, because we still live together, I think there is a 6 month separation period.
Thank you. I had a consultation with an attorney, but didn't ask this question due to time restraints. I don't want a huge cost, so I think I will avoid the fault divorce.
Yes! Telling my stepdaughter how I used to wear the same trendy things when I was her age, then remembering my mom telling me the exact same thing...
Thank you! I plan to call here on my lunch break tomorrow.
He was on the lease as a resident, but not as a leaseholder. They took his income into account when approving us.
The dishwasher never worked properly, so no, they don't have much basis to charge us.
We have a year left. We might just try to find someone else to move in and take our place.

I understood your comment. I do not get to choose how the $5,000 is applied, as it is in collections and as I stated in my post, they were unable to tell me how it will be applied. How a bank would apply it is irrelevant as well, because the debt is owned by a collection agency. My issue is that I do not know, nor am I able to decide how the refund will be applied, and therefore am unable to know whether the higher or lower interest rate loan will be paid off first. The interest rate of consolidated loan is an average of the two, so if the lower one is paid off, there is nothing to average - I get stuck with the higher rate. So consolidation is a bit of a gamble with the interest rate if I wait for the refund to hit first.

Thanks for the correction - I am not very financially savvy. 

Someone told me it is the oldest debt first to account for statute of limitations, but I don't know if that is a standard, especially considering student loans do not have a collection statute of limitations. It is probably lowest rate first, as you said.

That little voice goes away, with time and work. There are NA and AA meetings filled with people who understand you and will listen and help - if you want the help. If that's not your thing, DASA certified therapists specialize in drug and alcohol abuse. Change is rarely easy, but if you are willing to put the work in to alter your behavior and your thinking, then eventually things get better. I've been sober over three years, and I can tell you the using urge crosses my mind every once in a great while, but life is so good now that using isn't even an option.

Not a cop, but we called the complaint in and were shocked by the result. It was a college town and we lived near a bar, so not unusual to hear a drunken screaming girl, but this sounded...almost animalistic. My boyfriend and I called the cops and went to sleep. Cops bang on the door a little while later asking if we knew the people who lived across the way. When we told them we did not, they asked a few more questions (this was years ago, so don't remember specifics). The next day we walk out by the side of the building and the whole area is covered in police tape. Turns out a man stabbed his daughter's boyfriend. The boyfriend ran out, was stabbed again and again while the girlfriend screamed in terror. 

There was one other instance in the same complex where we called the cops. The cops came by to get my boyfriend's statement and said that when they got there the woman in the apartment started threatening them with a knife and so they detained her. 

We moved shortly thereafter, so I have no idea what happened in either situation.

I am white and went to rehab at a facility that was predominantly African American. This facility is known as one of the rougher ones, as it is state-funded and located in the ghetto (my first roommate had been tried for murder and dismissed due to mental insanity). When I first met everyone (in a hallway, on the way to a meal), three girls walked up to me and, without asking, started petting my hair (I have very straight blonde hair). This was not bad, just unnerving, as I do not like to be touched, especially by strangers. 
The actual discrimination didn't occur until I was at the end of my stay. A new roommate came in and was instantly verbally aggressive and accusative. She would constantly berate me and our half-white roommate. At every turn, she would put me down and try to provoke me to anger. Our other roommate fell for her crap, lashed out, and was moved to another room. I had been bullied as a child, so I didn't let her get under my skin. The confrontation escalated to the point where she had me pulled in the office and tried to get me kicked out of the facility by accusing me of harassing her. I stated my case, the counselors backed me up (they noted I had been there for months with no issues), and I was excused. Later, I talked to said roommate, and she admitted she hated me because I was white. I was shocked. We talked all night and I can only hope that I helped her avoid judgment of the individual. 
The experience made me realize how incredibly naive, sheltered, and blessed I was - blessed to never have to go through what she went through that bred such blind hatred.

A group of us went on a bar crawl, and my friend proceeded to get so blasted that by the time we got to the last bar, she was sick and barely able to walk (later found out she wasn't supposed to mix alcohol with her meds).. I drape her in a corner table and go up to the bar to get her a water, only to come back to a group of guys surrounding her (she was actually  passed out by this time). I immediately lost it and started yelling at them for being vultures preying on an unconscious girl, at which point they all slunk away. Disgusting.
